data.name: Wilhelmina
data.gender_notes: Wilhelmina is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Germanic elements wil, meaning 'will, desire', and helm, meaning 'helmet, protection'. The name Wilhelmina was popular among Germanic and Dutch royalty, as it conveyed the idea of a strong and determined ruler. In Christian tradition, Wilhelmina is associated with the virtues of faith and strength. The name Wilhelmina carries the meaning “Struggle, warrior” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, German, Dutch. Parents who choose Wilhelmina usually hope their child will grow to embody struggle, warrior and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name that embodies determination and faith in the face of challenges.
data.etymology: Wilhelmina belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Struggle, warrior.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Wilhelmina total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

in_hebrew.name: וילהלמינה
in_hebrew.meaning: אלוהים הוא הכתר שלי, רצון אלוהים
in_hebrew.long_meaning: וילהלמינה הוא שם נוצרי שמקורו בשם הגרמני 'וילהלם', שמורכב מהמילים 'ויל' שפירושה 'רצון' או 'החלטה' והמילה 'הלם' שפירושה 'קסדה' או 'מגן'. השם וילהלמינה הוא נגזרת נשית של השם וילהלם, ומשמעותו 'אלוהים הוא הכתר שלי' או 'רצון אלוהים'. השם וילהלמינה היה נפוץ בקרב הנוצרים בימי הביניים והוא עדיין בשימוש כיום.

in_greek.name: Βιλελμίνα
in_greek.long_meaning: Η Βιλελμίνα είναι ένα χριστιανικό όνομα που προέκυψε από το γερμανικό όνομα 'Βίλχελμ', το οποίο αποτελείται από τις λέξεις 'βίλ' που σημαίνει 'βούλησις' ή 'απόφαση' και τη λέξη 'χέλμ' που σημαίνει 'κράνος' ή 'ασπίδα'. Το όνομα Βιλελμίνα είναι η θηλυκή μορφή του ονόματος Βίλχελμ και σημαίνει 'Θεού βούλησις' ή 'στεφάνι του Θεού'. Το όνομα αυτό ήταν κοινό μεταξύ των χριστιανών κατά τον Μεσαίωνα και εξακολουθεί να χρησιμοποιείται σήμερα.

in_latin.name: Wilhelmina
in_latin.long_meaning: Wilhelmina est nomen christianum quod ex nomine germanico 'Wilhelmus' oritur, quod componitur ex vocibus 'wil' quae significat 'voluntas' seu 'decisio' et voce 'helm' quae significat 'cassis' seu 'scutum'. Nomen Wilhelmina est forma feminina nominis Wilhelmus et significat 'Dei voluntas' seu 'Corona Dei'. Hoc nomen inter christianos medio aevo usitatum erat et hodie etiam in usu est.

in_english.name: Wilhelmina
in_english.meaning: Resolute protector, God is my helmet
in_english.long_meaning: Wilhelmina is a Christian name derived from the Germanic name 'Wilhelm', which consists of the words 'wil' meaning 'will' or 'resolution' and 'helm' meaning 'helmet' or 'protector'. The name Wilhelmina is the feminine form of Wilhelm and signifies 'resolute protector' or 'God is my helmet'. This name was popular among Christians during the Middle Ages and is still used today, symbolizing strength, courage, and devotion to God.

data.cultural_impact: Wilhelmina was a common name among European royalty, particularly in Germany and the Netherlands. It was bestowed upon daughters of noble and regal lineages and reflected the expectations of power and strength.
data.spiritual_significance: Wilhelmina is a name deeply rooted in the Christian tradition, reflecting the virtues of faith and strength. The name is derived from the Germanic elements signifying 'will' and 'helmet', symbolizing one's unwavering determination to protect and uphold their beliefs, as well as to be steadfast in their convictions. Overall, Wilhelmina is a name that evokes a sense of courage, dedication, and spiritual conviction.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Wilhelmina: Strong-willed warrior of God. Derived from German elements meaning 'desiring will' or 'will helmet' - a name for those embracing God's will in strength and determination.

historical_references.reference: Born in the Netherlands in 1687, Wilhelmina was the daughter of William III of England and Mary II of Scotland.
historical_references.context: Wilhelmina was a Dutch princess who became the queen regnant of the Dutch Republic in 1890.
